newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-Doig dismisses ball tampering suggestions.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-Doig dismisses ball tampering suggestions.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Nov 20 - New Zealand Cricket chief executive Christopher Doig on Wednesday dismissed suggestions of ball tampering levelled at medium-fast bowler Simon Doull in Pakistan, NZPA reports.

Lahore-based newspaper The News published two photographs of Doull yesterday, with a caption speculating that he may have been using the nail on his right thumb to disfigure one side of the ball. It asked the ICC match referee to take note of the action.
Doig said today he had spoken to the team management and was satisfied that Doull was not involved in any sinister activity.
"I've not seen the picture, but I have spoken to the management and Earle Cooper (manager) assures me that he assumes the picture was entirely mischievous," Doig said.
"He has been told by Doull that he was doing nothing more than cleaning dirt off the ball."
Cooper has already rejected suggestions that any of his players would tamper with the ball.
"New Zealand cricketers are not cheats," Cooper said in Pakistan.
"We are concerned that the suggestion should be raised of ball tampering.
"It is not a practice of New Zealand cricketers.
"Simon was simply cleaning dirt off the ball. The ground here is very sandy and dirt often clings to the ball."
Doig said while he wasn't surprised by the incident, he wasn't happy about it.
"It is disappointing, we'd rather just try to keep our minds on having them getting on with the game," he said.
"It is not surprising that it happened, but at the same time I am not overly concerned by it."

The suggestions are ironic in that Pakistan's bowlers have in recent years come under increasing scrutiny for ball tampering, an issue first raised during New Zealand's last tour to that country in 1990.
Similar concerns were raised when Pakistan were in New Zealand in 1993-94 by then New Zealand captain, the outspoken Ken Rutherford who is now in South Africa.
